name: Udi
catalog_quote: 2.1.2. Ударение – силовое, динамическое; падает на последний слог (в имени); вызывает редукцию безударного гласного (напр. жогъул 'лето' – жогъла 'летом'); в многосложном глаголе два ударения – в начале и в конце, ср. аш-не-беса 'работает'. Долгота гласного также может иметь фонологический характер: эхне 'говорит' – э:хне 'говорит без конца, долго'; унекса 'ест' – у:некса 'ест без конца, жадно'.

audit.recode_to: fixed-dominant (final): keep final as the default position but drop strict=true. All three specialist sources hedge: Dzheiranishvili 2001 limits final stress to nouns ('в имени') and gives verbs two stresses; Talibov & Maisak 2005 p.181 say stress 'also occurs on the first syllable' (ттéсагьат, мéтаьр) and 'no clear rules governing stress have been identified'; Schulze 2001 §2.5 says the final syllable is stressed 'in many instances', with clitics unstressed and some particles inherently stressed. Also populate quote/cite/loc/grade from dq/dloc (currently empty) and add Talibov & Maisak 2005 p.181 and Schulze 2001 §2.5 as corroborating citations.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified on the held scan at printed p.454 §2.1.2 (image-only PDF; scanned + page image). (2) Deciding source is a 2001 encyclopedic sketch; the held Talibov & Maisak 2005 sketch (Maisak is the leading current Udi fieldworker) and Schulze's 2001 online grammar §2.5, fetched sources now from the Wayback Machine, independently confirm predominantly final dynamic stress, so the position coding is safe. (3) But every source qualifies the rule (initial stress in deictic-containing words, double stress in polysyllabic verbs, pre-clitic stress, 'no clear rules identified'), so 'fixed-strict' overstates the descriptions; 'fixed-dominant' final matches them. (4) The open-access Gippert & Dum-Tragut 2023 handbook (fetched sources, 753 pp) has no modern-Udi stress rule. sources.citation: Schulze, Wolfgang. 2001. The Udi Language: A grammatical description with sample text (online grammar, LMU Munich), ch. 2 'Phonological system', §2.5 Stress. Wayback snapshot 2009-09-04 of http://www.lrz-muenchen.de/~wschulze/udiphon.htm
sources.quote: 'Today, the stress pattern of Udi resembles that of Azeri (historically, Udi had its words stressed on the first or second syllable). In many instances, the final syllable is stressed. Yet, a considerable number of en- or endoclitics provoke the accentuation of the preceding syllable (cf. section 3.3.3 for personal agreement clitics). Some particles call for a clitic because of their inherent stress, e.g. q'a- (adh), gi- (cond), te- (neg), e.g. téne baksà, bürmišq'áq'un bi, campegízui.'

sources.quote: No statement of the modern Udi word-stress rule. Ch.4 §2.2.3: 'Nothing is known about the prosodic features of Albanian… suggests that the language was characterised by some kind of stress accent.' Ch.5 §3.2.4 on endoclitics: clitic placement 'induced a preference for the clitic to enter into a position after the first accented syllable of the verbal complex'.
